description: Health of the Envoy Gateway edge proxy: what to act on first, then the drill-down. Source: oci/envoy-gateway in gitops-manifests.

panels.title: Act now - every panel here is a future alert

options.content: **Red means act.** Each tile is the basis for an alert. Windows are fixed (not the time picker) so the tile matches what an alert would evaluate. SLO: **availability ${slo}**, **p99 < ${latency_slo}s**. *Envoy-generated 5xx* are errors the proxy produced itself (no healthy endpoint, connect failure, timeout, overflow) - the backend never answered. Drill down in **Upstream / routes**.

panels.description: HPA desired replicas minus available proxy pods. Non-zero for more than a few minutes means pods are not starting or not ready (image pull, scheduling, crash loop).
panels.title: Missing proxies

panels.description: Share of client requests that did not get a 5xx, last hour, all listeners in the filter. Red below the SLO.
panels.title: Availability (1h)

panels.description: SLO window. Red below the SLO target.
panels.title: Availability (30d)

panels.description: 1 = untouched, 0 = spent. Below 0 the SLO is breached for the window.
panels.title: Error budget left (30d)

panels.description: Client-observed p99, from Envoy's downstream request time histogram (ms). Red above the latency SLO.
panels.title: p99 latency (5m)

panels.description: Share of requests where Envoy returned a 5xx the backend did not: downstream 5xx minus upstream 5xx. Typical causes: UH no healthy endpoint, UF connect failure, UT route timeout, UO overflow. Approximate - retries can make upstream counts exceed downstream, so it is clamped at 0.
panels.title: Envoy-generated 5xx (5m)

panels.description: Route rules (Envoy clusters) whose backends have zero healthy endpoints - every request to them is a 503 UH. Includes Services scaled to 0. See 'Routes' table for which.
panels.title: Routes without healthy endpoints

panels.description: Soonest-expiring certificate served by any listener, including ListenerSet team certs. The platform cert is synced from Key Vault hourly by External Secrets - a value that keeps falling means rotation or sync is stuck. See 'TLS certificates' row.
panels.title: Min TLS cert days left

panels.description: Requests let through because the global rate limit service did not answer (failClosed: false). Nothing else moves when this happens - the global limit is silently off. Check envoy-ratelimit pods, Valkey, and the valkey NetworkPolicy.
panels.title: Rate limit fail-open (15m)

panels.description: Proxies that lost their xDS stream to envoy-gateway. They keep serving their last config, but no route, cert or endpoint change reaches them.
panels.title: Proxies disconnected from xDS

panels.description: xDS updates Envoy refused (CDS/LDS/RDS update_rejected on the proxy, xds_nack_total on the controller). The proxy keeps the previous config - recent Gateway API changes are not live. Check envoy-gateway logs for the rejected resource.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(cluster_manager_cds_update_rejected_total{k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}[15m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(listener_manager_lds_update_rejected_total{k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}[15m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(http_rds_update_rejected_total{k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}[15m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(xds_nack_total{k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}[15m])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Config rejected (15m)

panels.description: Clients turned away: ClientTrafficPolicy connectionLimit, the 50k global connection limit, or the overload manager shedding load. Scale out or find the client.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(listener_downstream_cx_overflow_total{k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}[15m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(listener_downstream_global_cx_overflow_total{k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}[15m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(listener_downstream_cx_overload_reject_total{k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}[15m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(http_downstream_rq_overload_close_total{k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}[15m])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Connections rejected (15m)

panels.description: Busiest proxy pod's connections as a share of the bootstrap global_downstream_max_connections (50000 per pod). At 100% new connections are refused.
panels.title: Connections vs 50k limit

panels.description: At 100% the HPA cannot add capacity - CPU climbs and latency follows.
panels.title: Replicas vs HPA max

panels.description: Envoy container restarts. Memory limit equals request, so OOMKill is the usual cause.
panels.title: Proxy restarts (1h)

panels.description: envoy-ratelimit scrape and Valkey (redis_up). Needs an otel-collector prometheus receiver (see the oci/envoy-gateway README). No data = not scraped yet.
panels.title: Global rate limiter up

panels.description: Available envoy-gateway controller replicas. At 0 nothing reconciles - existing proxies keep serving, but no change goes out and new proxies cannot start.
panels.title: Controller

panels.description: Current client request rate. A sudden drop to near zero with no errors usually means traffic is not reaching the edge at all (DNS, load balancer, public IP).
panels.title: Requests / s

panels.description: Multi-window burn rate (Google SRE workbook): page - 2% of the 30d budget in 1h. An alert fires when BOTH windows are above 14.4x. 1x = spending the budget exactly over 30 days.
panels.title: Page: 1h & 5m burn

panels.description: Multi-window burn rate (Google SRE workbook): page - 5% of the 30d budget in 6h. An alert fires when BOTH windows are above 6x. 1x = spending the budget exactly over 30 days.
panels.title: Page: 6h & 30m burn

panels.description: Multi-window burn rate (Google SRE workbook): ticket - 10% of the 30d budget in 3d. An alert fires when BOTH windows are above 1x. 1x = spending the budget exactly over 30 days.
panels.title: Ticket: 3d & 6h burn

panels.description: Error ratio divided by the error budget (1 - SLO). Threshold lines at 6x and 14.4x - the page thresholds.
panels.title: Burn rate

panels.description: From the le="1000" (ms) bucket of the downstream request time histogram. The SLO line is the target (p99 < 1s means at least 99% here).
panels.title: Latency SLI - share of requests under ${latency_slo}s

panels.description: Client requests per second by status class.
panels.title: Requests by response class

panels.description: 5xx counts against the SLO. A 4xx spike without a deploy usually means a client or bot (or a rate limit kicking in - 429).
panels.title: Error ratio

panels.description: Client-observed request time, first byte in to last byte out (ms).
panels.title: Latency

panels.description: Downstream request time buckets.
panels.title: Latency distribution

panels.description: Per HTTP connection manager (http-<port> / https-<port>).
panels.title: Requests by listener

panels.description: Open client connections. Uneven pods point at long-lived connections pinned by the LB (externalTrafficPolicy: Local).
panels.title: Active connections per pod

panels.description: TLS handshakes are the expensive part of a new connection - the real capacity number. TLS errors: clients with unsupported versions/ciphers (minVersion 1.2) or scanners.
panels.title: New connections / TLS handshakes

panels.description: Each counter belongs to exactly one ClientTrafficPolicy timeout, so a spike says which limit clients ran into. Per listener, not per route.
panels.title: Timeouts by setting

panels.description: Unknown SNI = a hostname nobody serves: typo, DNS pointing here, or a ListenerSet that was not accepted.
panels.title: Protocol abuse & misrouting

panels.description: One row per route rule (Envoy cluster httproute/<ns>/<name>/rule/<n>), last 5m. Sorted by 5xx. UH/UF/UT/UO are Envoy-generated failures: no healthy endpoint, connect failure, route timeout, overflow. Healthy endpoints is summed over proxy pods (each pod sees every endpoint), so compare it to itself over time, not to the pod count.
panels.title: Routes - worst first

panels.description: Response-flag equivalents per route, from counters (Envoy exports no response-flag stats). Only non-zero series are drawn. UT route timeout is Envoy's 15s default unless the HTTPRoute sets timeouts.request. UC usually means the backend's keepalive timeout is shorter than Envoy's.
panels.title: Envoy-generated failures by cause

panels.description: 5xx returned by backends (plus Envoy-generated ones attributed to the cluster).
panels.title: Upstream 5xx ratio by route (top 10)

panels.description: Backend response time as seen by Envoy (ms).
panels.title: Upstream p99 by route (top 10)

panels.description: Endpoints not taking traffic, summed over proxy pods. Excluded/ejected only appear once a BackendTrafficPolicy configures active or passive health checks.
panels.title: Endpoints

panels.description: Only produced once a BackendTrafficPolicy configures retries. A rising retry rate amplifies load on an already struggling backend.
panels.title: Retries

panels.description: 1 while a circuit breaker is tripped on any proxy. Envoy's defaults (1024 connections/requests per cluster per pod) apply even without a BackendTrafficPolicy.
panels.title: Circuit breakers open

panels.description: The catch-all local limit from backend-traffic-policy.yaml. In-process, no backing store - the survival ceiling while the global limiter is unavailable.
panels.title: Local rate limit (per pod, 10000 rps per route)

panels.description: As seen by Envoy. error and FAIL-OPEN mean the ratelimit service did not answer within 20ms and the request was let through. Empty until a BackendTrafficPolicy uses rateLimit.global.
panels.title: Global rate limit - filter view

panels.description: From the envoy-ratelimit service (needs the otel-collector scrape, see the README). The domain is the listener or shared policy. Counters gain _total in remote write like every other counter.
panels.title: Global rate limit - service view

panels.description: Valkey holds only rate-limit counters. Memory limit equals VALKEY_MEMORY_REQUEST.
panels.title: Valkey memory

panels.description: Evictions mean counters are lost early - rate limits become more lenient.
panels.title: Valkey load

panels.description: Single replica on emptyDir: every restart resets all global rate-limit counters.
panels.title: Valkey restarts

panels.description: HPA 3-20 on 50% CPU, scale-down waits 15 minutes. Desired pinned at max = out of headroom.
panels.title: Proxy replicas

panels.description: No CPU limit by design. The HPA targets 50% of the request.
panels.title: CPU per proxy pod

panels.description: Limit equals ENVOY_MEMORY_REQUEST. Hitting it is an OOMKill.
panels.title: Memory per proxy pod

panels.description: Envoy's own view of its memory. Allocated growing without traffic growth suggests a leak or connection buildup.
panels.title: Envoy heap

panels.description: Overload manager refuses new connections at 50000 per pod.
panels.title: Connections per pod vs global limit

panels.description: 0-1. The fixed_heap monitor is only active if a max heap size is configured.
panels.title: Overload manager pressure

panels.description: Config a proxy refused. The proxy keeps its previous config. The controller log names the resource. New in Envoy Gateway v1.9.
panels.title: xDS NACKs by proxy

panels.description: The proxy side of the same event.
panels.title: Config rejected (proxy side)

panels.description: Clusters waiting for endpoints before going active. Non-zero for long blocks listener updates.
panels.title: Warming clusters

panels.description: Failures writing Gateway API status or creating the proxy Deployment/Service/HPA. Panics are bugs - the controller recovered, but that runner's work was lost.
panels.title: Reconcile failures

panels.description: Work waiting per runner. A depth that keeps climbing means the controller is not keeping up with changes.
panels.title: Watchable queue depth

panels.description: envoy-gateway controller container.
panels.title: Controller resources

panels.description: Every certificate served by any listener, including ListenerSet team certs. Platform cert: Key Vault -> External Secrets (hourly) -> tls-cert Secret.
panels.title: Certificates by expiry
